assumptions: The state is wickets lost and ball age only. Match situation, innings number, venue, declarations and the follow-on are ignored, which overstates run expectancy for strong positions (ADR-011).
A new ball is taken every 80 overs, so ball age wraps from 80 back to 1.
The innings ends only when ten wickets have fallen.
Every ball's wicket probability and mean runs depend only on the current wickets lost and ball age.
Every kind of dismissal counts as a wicket, except retirements.
An over is six legal balls. Runs and wickets from wides and no-balls are counted in their (wickets lost, ball age) cell and divided by that cell's legal balls.
Rates in sparse cells are smoothed: each (wickets lost, ball age) cell is shrunk towards the rate for its wickets lost over all ball ages, with a prior weight of 1200 legal balls.
